nodes.name: NiFe-MOFs Solvothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFe-MOFs are prepared using a solvothermal method by coordinating Ni and Fe precursors with BDC.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, the NiFe-MOFs are also prepared using a similar method.

properties.description: 3D framework structure with metal nodes and organic linkers

nodes.source_text: IrNi@NiFe-MOFs exhibit superior OER performance, requiring only a low overpotential of 228 mV to achieve a current density of 10 mA cm−2 which is superior to IrNi (255 mV), NiFe-MOFs (343 mV), and IrO2 (287 mV)... Tafel slope (37.6 mV dec−1)... interfacial charge-transfer resistance (7.6 Ω)... Cdl values of NiFe-MOFs and IrNi@NiFe-MOFs are calculated to be 2.0 and 2.2 mF cm−2... 7.2-fold enhancement... TOF value of 0.160 s−1... excellent oxygen production rate without obvious degradation for 40 h... 115 h under 100 mA cm−2... faradaic efficiency of 96%
commercial IrO2 (287 mV) ... (58.0 mV dec−1) ... (19.7 Ω)
NiFe-MOFs (343 mV)... (102.9 mV dec−1)... (90.4 Ω)... Cdl values ... 2.0 ... rapid activity attenuation within 14 h

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of IrNi@NiFe-MOFs and NiFe-MOFs match simulated NiFe-MOFs with diffraction peaks at 8.9°, 14.2°, 16.0°, and 17.9° corresponding to (200), (001), (201), and (400) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of NiFe-MOFs and IrNi@NiFe-MOFs are displayed in Figure 1b. Both have almost the same crystalline structure that matches well with the simulated NiFe-MOFs with diffraction peaks at 8.9, 14.2, 16.0, and 17.9° corresponding to the (200), (001), (201) and (400) planes...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra confirm BDC coordination with metal ions in NiFe-MOFs and IrNi@NiFe-MOFs, showing slight peak shifts compared to BDC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectroscopy of BDC shows the carboxylate group's (−COO−)' stretching modes at 1450 and 1629 cm−1 ... However, compared with the BDC, the peaks of NiFe-MOFs and IrNi@NiFe-MOFs exhibit a slight shift...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows IrNi nanoalloys (≈3.29±0.12 nm) uniformly dispersed on NiFe-MOFs nanosheets; HRTEM displays lattice fringes of 2.04 Å (103) and 2.18 Å (111) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Abundant IrNi nanoalloys (red circles) with a diameter averaging 3.29±0.12 nm are uniformly dispersed on the NiFe-MOFs nanosheet (Figure 1d). ... the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) displays distinct lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of 2.04 and 2.18 Å (Figure 1f,g), corresponding to the (103) and (111) planes...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-MOFs BET surface area 329.6 m² g⁻¹, IrNi@NiFe-MOFs 118.9 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N₂ adsorption/desorption measurements reveal that NiFe-MOFs have a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area of 329.6 m² g⁻¹, which is higher than that of IrNi@NiFe-MOFs (118.9 m² g⁻¹)...

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS of IrNi@NiFe-MOFs: Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺ at 856.2/873.8 eV and Ni⁰ at 852.6 eV; Fe 2p shows Fe³⁺ shifted positively and new Fe²⁺ at 710.2/723.2 eV; Ir 4f shows Ir⁰ at 60.8/64.0 eV and Ir-O at 62.0/65.4 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of NiFe-MOFs (Figure 1i) exhibits two characteristic peaks at 856.2 and 873.8 eV ... However, IrNi@NiFe-MOFs displays a new peak at 852.6 eV corresponding to Ni⁰ ... In the high-resolution Fe 2p XPS spectrum (Figure 1j), ... two new Fe²⁺ peaks at 710.2 and 723.2 eV ... In the Ir 4f spectrum (Figure 1k), the peaks at 60.8 and 64.0 eV correspond to the Ir⁰ 4f7/2 and Ir⁰ 4f5/2...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows phase transformation NiFe-MOFs → NiFe(OH)₂ → NiFeOOH; IrNi@NiFe-MOFs transforms faster with Fe-O bond elongation and Ni³⁺-O peaks at lower potential (1.42 V).
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the applied potential is set to 1.03 V, the Raman spectrum of NiFe-MOFs displays four peaks at about 450, 528, 680, and 1350 cm⁻¹ ... Two new peaks at ≈475 and 551 cm⁻¹ emerge when the applied potential is increased to 1.43 V, which are assigned to the E_g bending vibration and the A_{1g} tensile vibration of Ni^{III}-O in NiFeOOH...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER TEM of IrNi@NiFeOOH shows maintained IrNi nanoparticles (2.04/2.19 Å lattice) on NiFeOOH nanosheets (2.10 Å, 102 plane).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image of IrNi@NiFeOOH (Figure 4b) not only exhibits the lattice fringes of NiFeOOH (2.10 Å indexed to (102) planes) but also shows the lattice fringes of IrNi nanoalloys (2.19 and 2.04 Å corresponding to (111) and (103) planes)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS of IrNi@NiFeOOH: Ni 2p Ni³⁺ peaks shift -0.3 eV to lower binding energy with Ni⁰ at 852.5 eV; Fe 2p Fe³⁺ peaks shift +0.2 eV; Ir 4f shows Ir⁰ and Ir-O peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of NiFeOOH (Figure 4f) displays two characteristic peaks of Ni³⁺, 2p1/2 and Ni³⁺, 2p3/2 at 873.9 and 856.2 eV ... Compared to NiFeOOH, IrNi@NiFeOOH shows a new peak at 852.5 eV corresponding to Ni⁰. More importantly, the Ni³⁺, 2p1/2 and Ni³⁺, 2p3/2 peaks of IrNi@NiFeOOH shift toward low binding energy (0.3 eV) ... In the high-resolution Fe 2p XPS spectrum of NiFeOOH (Figure 4g), ... the Fe 2p1/2 and Fe 2p3/2 peaks for IrNi@NiFeOOH show a slight shift by 0.2 eV toward higher binding energy...

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES shows Ni oxidation state lower in IrNi@NiFeOOH vs NiFeOOH; Fe average valence 2.50 (NiFeOOH) to 3.25 (IrNi@NiFeOOH); Ir valence +1.33.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni K-edge XANES spectra (Figure 5a), the absorption edges of NiFeOOH and IrNi@NiFeOOH shift toward positive energy compared to that of NiO ... For the Fe K-edge XANES spectra (Figure 5d), ... the average valence states of Fe in NiFeOOH and IrNi@NiFeOOH are ≈2.50 and 3.25...

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows shortened Ni-O/Fe-O bonds in IrNi@NiFeOOH vs NiFeOOH; Ir-Ni at 2.54 Å, Ir-O at 1.98 Å confirming Ni/Fe-O-Ir interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra ... display that the peaks at ≈1.57 and 2.75 Å are indexed to the first shell of Ni-O ... For Ir elements in IrNi@NiFeOOH, ... a predominant peak at 2.54 Å (fitted value) ... the presence of Ir-O bonds (1.98 Å)...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP confirms IrNi@NiFe-MOFs composition: Ni 30.6 wt%, Fe 12.5 wt%, Ir 0.33 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ICP analysis reveals that the contents of Ni and Fe in IrNi@NiFe-MOFs are similar to those of NiFe-MOFs. Specifically, the contents of Ni, Fe, and Ir in IrNi@NiFe-MOFs are 30.6, 12.5, and 0.33 wt.%, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows IrNi@NiFe-MOFs maintains 3D micro-flower morphology assembled by ultrathin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images reveal that the Ir_xNi@NiFe-MOFs present a 3D micro-flower structure assembled by several ultrathin nanosheets (Figure S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms IrNi nanoalloy lattice fringes at 2.04 Å (103 plane) and 2.18 Å (111 plane) in IrNi@NiFe-MOFs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) displays distinct lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of 2.04 and 2.18 Å (Figure 1f,g), corresponding to the (103) and (111) planes of IrNi nanoalloy, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms polycrystalline IrNi nanoalloys in IrNi@NiFe-MOFs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selective area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern further suggests the formation of IrNi nanoalloys (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: HADDF-STEM and elemental mapping show uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Ir, O, C in IrNi@NiFe-MOFs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HADDF-STEM image and corresponding elemental mapping show the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Ir, O, and C elements in IrNi@NiFe-MOFs (Figure 1h)...
